title: How much milk was supplied in the last three days?
description: Milk supplied over the first three days is added with the points lined up, and the total is taken away from the six day total. Twenty five is written with zeroes after the point so the break can be made. The answer is checked by adding the two parts back.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the known days, then take that total away from the whole to find the missing part. Watch for students who forget to write the whole number with zeroes after the point.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q8
video_script.why: The child can add and subtract decimals with breaking, and now uses both in one story about milk.
video_script.substitution: Add the known amounts with the points in one column, then take that total away from the whole.
video_script.anchor: Milk supplied to a dairy, in three amounts over the first three days and a total over six days.
video_script.payoff_line: Take the part already known away from the whole
maths_rules: units 3 + 4 + 4 + 1 = 12, so the first three days total 12.24 L
last three days = 25 - 12.24 = 12.76 L, with 25 written as 25.00
25.00 breaks into 24 units, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths: 10 - 4 = 6, 9 - 2 = 7, 24 - 12 = 12
video_script.design: The three amounts sit in a column with the points aligned and the second written as 4.20. The total of the first three days is taken from 25.00 in a second column, then the two parts are added back to reach 25.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; milk cans with 3.79 L, 4.2 L, 4.25 L for the first three days, 25 L for six days, and a question mark for the last three days

marks.scene: the title card From your book arrives
marks.days: three milk cans appear for the first three days
marks.amounts: the cans are labelled 3.79 L, 4.2 L and 4.25 L
marks.six: a big can labelled 25 L appears for six days
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the last three days

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about milk sent to a dairy.
<bookmark mark='days'/>In the first three days, {{NAME_6}} supplies three amounts of milk.
<bookmark mark='amounts'/>They are three point seven nine litres, four point two litres and four point two five litres.
<bookmark mark='six'/>In six days, {{NAME_6}} supplies twenty five litres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much milk is supplied in the last three days?

beats.on_screen: the milk cans stay on the board with the question mark

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: decimals stacked with points in one column; 4.2 written as 4.20; a bar split into a known part and a missing part

marks.add: decimals are stacked with their points in one column
marks.part: a bar shows a known part and a missing part

beats.colours: the known part and the missing part in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>To add decimals, keep the point of each number in one column.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>A short decimal can be written with a zero at the end.
<bookmark mark='part'/>A missing part is found by taking the known part away from the whole.

beats.on_screen: Given: first three days 3.79 L, 4.2 L, 4.25 L; six days 25 L

marks.given: the words Given and three days are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three amounts in the first three days.
<bookmark mark='amounts'/>They are three point seven nine, four point two and four point two five litres.
<bookmark mark='six'/>In six days, the supply is twenty five litres.

beats.on_screen: To find: milk supplied in the last three days

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the milk supplied in the last three days.

marks.stack: 3.79, 4.2 and 4.25 are stacked with the points in one column

beats.colours: the added zero in a new colour
narration: <bookmark mark='stack'/>Step one, write the three amounts one under the other, with the point in one column.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Four point two becomes four point two zero, so every amount has two places.

beats.on_screen: hundredths: 9 + 0 + 5 = 14, write 4 carry 1; tenths: 7 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1; units: 3 + 4 + 4 + 1 = 12; total 12.24 L

marks.u: 3 + 4 + 4 + 1 = 12 is written to the left of the 2
marks.total: 12.24 L is boxed as the first three days

beats.colours: the carried digits in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one ten moves left as a carry
narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step two, add the three amounts, starting at the right.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Hundredths: nine plus zero plus five is fourteen. Write four and carry one.
<bookmark mark='t'/>Tenths: seven plus two plus two plus one is twelve. Write two and carry one.
<bookmark mark='u'/>Units: three plus four plus four plus one is twelve.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The first three days total twelve point two four litres.

marks.rule: 25 - 12.24 is written under the label last three days

beats.colours: the added zeroes in a new colour
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, the last three days are the six day total take away twelve point two four.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Write twenty five as twenty five point zero zero.

beats.on_screen: 25.00 becomes 24 units, 9 tenths, 10 hundredths; hundredths 10 - 4 = 6; tenths 9 - 2 = 7; units 24 - 12 = 12

marks.break: 25.00 is rewritten as 24 units, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths
marks.h: 10 - 4 = 6 is written in the hundredths column
marks.t: 9 - 2 = 7 is written in the tenths column
marks.u: 24 - 12 = 12 is written in the units columns

beats.colours: the broken unit in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one unit moves right as ten tenths, then one tenth as ten hundredths
narration: <bookmark mark='break'/>Step four, twenty five point zero zero is twenty four units, nine tenths and ten hundredths.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Hundredths: ten take away four is six.
<bookmark mark='t'/>Tenths: nine take away two is seven.
<bookmark mark='u'/>Units: twenty four take away twelve is twelve.

beats.on_screen: check: add the digits 6 + 4, 7 + 2 + 1, 12 + 12 + 1 column by column; the sum is 25.00

marks.check: the two parts are stacked to be added

beats.colours: the carried digits in a new colour
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check by adding the two parts back. They must make twenty five.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Hundredths: six plus four is ten. Write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='t'/>Tenths: seven plus two plus one is ten. Write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='u'/>Units: twelve plus twelve plus one is twenty five, so the parts make twenty five.

marks.payoff: the rule is written above the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Take the part already known away from the whole.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_6}} supplies twelve point seven six litres in the last three days.
